newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end abbreviated day mixed, yen firms.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end abbreviated day mixed, yen firms.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed an abbreviated session mixed, as a stronger yen led traders to unwind long sterling and Canadian dollar cash positions against the Japanese currency, traders and analysts said.
December yen set a new session high before its early close on Monday at 1200 CST/1800 GMT and helped push December Canadian dollars further below support at $0.7512.

Meanwhile, December marks spiked higher, jumping above a two-month high at $0.6701 late due to options-related buying. One trader said a barrier option in cash at 1.4950 spot was touched off minutes before IMM pit trade closed.
Earlier dealer buying in marks and Swiss francs sparked a local short-covering rally, and helped December retrace more than 50 percent of its decline from July to October.
The late rally drove December closer to retracing 62-percent of its 4-1/2-month losses. The 62-percent Fibonacci retracement level is at $0.6736, analysts said.
December marks also closed above $0.6700, which signals a possible reversal in the contract's intermediate-term downtrend, a technical analyst said.
The downtrend in Swiss francs remains intact, as December rose slightly above the one-week high at $0.7958.
December Swiss francs rose to $0.7965, as the dollar quickly slipped through 1.26 spot.

Several traders said they are looking for December yen to continue to rise in the short-term. Resistance is at $0.009067, which is roughly equivalent to 110.50 spot yen, and $0.009135, or 110.00 spot in the near term. The contract's 1-1/2-month high is $0.009097.
Late in the day, the contract rose to $0.009055, slightly above its previous high of $0.009053, as the dollar ground below 111.00 spot.

Traders said the market was slightly concerned that Japan's Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara failed to negate his statement last week that the dollar's upward correction against the yen may be over.
Sakakibara said overnight that a revised forex policy would likely be implemented in the summer of 1997, and Japan welcomes developments in forex since April 1995.
They also said the absence of the U.S. administration's reiteration of strong dollar comments was also weighing on the U.S. dollar.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was up $0.000069 at $0.009053, marks were up $0.0047 at $0.6710, Swiss francs were up $0.0060 at $0.7991, sterling was flat at $1.6466, Canadian dollars were off $0.0020 at $0.7512, Australian dollars were $0.0010 lower at $0.7856 and Mexican pesos were $0.000125 lower at $0.123450. -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
